title: Build a Stage 5 Computing Showcase
overview: Bring together everything from Stage 5 Computing into one showcase: a working program, the data behind it, a clear explanation of how it runs, and the safety rules you followed while making it.

project.drivingQuestion: How can I use the computing I learned in Stage 5 to build something that solves a real problem for someone in my community — and explain exactly how it works?
project.finalProduct: A working program or digital product, the plan and algorithm behind it, a test-and-debug log, a data display, and a spoken or written explanation of your design decisions.

stages.title: 1. Plan and decompose
stages.prompt: Choose a real problem. Using the ideas from Units 1, 2, break it into smaller parts and write the algorithm before you write any code.
stages.evidence: A decomposed problem and a written algorithm or flowchart

stages.title: 2. Build it
stages.prompt: Build your program or product using the tools from Units 3, 4. Build the smallest working version first, then add one feature at a time.
stages.evidence: A working program or digital product

stages.title: 3. Test, debug and improve
stages.prompt: Test your work against your success criteria. Keep a log of every bug: what you saw, what caused it, and how you fixed it.
stages.evidence: A test-and-debug log with at least three entries

stages.title: 4. Share it safely
stages.prompt: Present your showcase. Explain three design decisions, show your data, and say which online-safety rules from Units 1, 2, 3, 4 you followed and why.
stages.evidence: A spoken, written or recorded explanation covering design, data and safety

evidenceChecklist: A decomposed problem with a written algorithm or flowchart
A working program or digital product
A test-and-debug log with at least three fixed bugs
Success criteria, each one ticked off with evidence
An explanation of your design decisions and the safety rules you followed

rubric.secure: The problem is decomposed, the algorithm is precise, and the pattern behind it is named.
The program runs, meets its criteria, and every bug found is logged with its cause and fix.
Data is collected accurately, organised sensibly and displayed so it answers a question.
Personal information is protected, sources are credited, and safety choices are explained.

questions.question: What is a variable?
options: a fixed number
a named box that stores a value that can change
a type of loop
a sound
questions.answer: a named box that stores a value that can change
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: 1 (b) a named box that stores a value that can change. That is exactly what a variable is.

questions.question: What does decomposition mean?
options: deleting code
breaking a big problem into smaller parts
repeating a loop
hiding a variable
questions.answer: breaking a big problem into smaller parts
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: 7 (b) breaking a big problem into smaller parts. That is decomposition.

questions.question: Success criteria are:
options: bugs in the code
the list of things a program must do to be a success
the user's score
a type of loop
questions.answer: the list of things a program must do to be a success
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: 12 (b) the list of things a program must do to be a success.

questions.question: What does “analyse” mean in computing?
options: To look closely at data, find patterns, and think about what it means.
Done by itself, with no human help (as a data logger records readings).
A middle value; add all the values and divide by how many there are. Also called the mean.
A line on a chart. The x axis is horizontal; the y axis is vertical.
questions.answer: To look closely at data, find patterns, and think about what it means.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Analyse means to look closely at data, find patterns, and think about what it means..

questions.question: What does “bar chart” mean in computing?
options: A chart with a bar for each category; the longer the bar, the greater the value.
Data grouped into categories, often words, such as favourite fruit.
One box in a spreadsheet grid, where a row and a column meet.
A cell's address, made of its column letter and row number, such as B3.
questions.answer: A chart with a bar for each category; the longer the bar, the greater the value.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Axis means a line on a chart. The x axis is horizontal; the y axis is vertical.

questions.question: Which computing word matches this meaning: Numerical data that can take any value in a range, such as temperature.?
options: continuous data
continuously
data
data logger
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Chart means a picture of data that makes patterns easy to see.

questions.question: What does “network” mean in computing?
options: A group of computers and devices connected together so they can share data, files and devices.
The physical machines and parts of a computer system that you can touch.
A wire used to connect a device to a network.
A device that connects wired devices together on one network.
questions.answer: A group of computers and devices connected together so they can share data, files and devices.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Network means a group of computers and devices connected together so they can share data, files and devices.

questions.question: What does “router” mean in computing?
options: A device that connects one network to another network — most often to the internet.
A device that lets computers join a network without wires, using Wi-Fi.
A part that sends and receives wireless signals.
A way of connecting devices to a network without wires, over a short distance.
questions.answer: A device that connects one network to another network — most often to the internet.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Router means a device that connects one network to another network — most often to the internet.

questions.question: Which computing word matches this meaning: A wireless network that uses tall towers to cover very large areas (4G and 5G).?
options: cellular network
range
interference
server
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Cellular network means a wireless network that uses tall towers to cover very large areas (4G and 5G).

questions.question: What does “input” mean in computing?
options: Data that goes into a computer to tell it what is happening.
Hardware that provides input to a computer, for example a keyboard.
Information or an action that comes out of a computer after processing.
Hardware that produces output, for example a screen or a printer.
questions.answer: Data that goes into a computer to tell it what is happening.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Input means data that goes into a computer to tell it what is happening.

questions.question: What does “sensor” mean in computing?
options: An input device that senses and measures changes around it, such as heat, light or movement.
An output device that moves, opens, closes or controls a physical object.
Far away; a remote device connects to a computer over the internet.
Working without a human doing it each time.
questions.answer: An input device that senses and measures changes around it, such as heat, light or movement.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Sensor means an input device that senses and measures changes around it, such as heat, light or movement.

questions.question: Which computing word matches this meaning: A device that lets a computer save data, even when the power is off.?
options: storage device
internal storage device
external storage device
magnetic storage device
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Storage device means a device that lets a computer save data, even when the power is off.
